skill.name: caveman-setup
skill.description: Configure repository LLM clients to use Caveman Cloud for spend measurement, then verify the integration with one real request.
skill.summary: Routes supported LLM call sites through Caveman Cloud and reports measured usage.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: Most command, environment-file, and secret-name alerts are documentation false positives. Confirmed risks include third-party routing of LLM data, BYOK provider credential exposure, mutable remote instructions, and an automatic billable verification request.

remediation.issue: LLM content and BYOK provider keys pass through a third-party gateway.
remediation.suggestion: Require informed confirmation before rerouting traffic, disclose data handling, and prefer scoped, revocable credentials with restrictive provider limits.

remediation.issue: The skill makes one real billable request without a separate confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination, model, credential mode, and estimated cost, then require confirmation before sending the verification request.

remediation.issue: Framework instructions may be fetched from mutable remote documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin documentation to an immutable revision and verify its content hash before following repository modification instructions.

content.user_title: Route LLM Calls Through Caveman Cloud
content.value_statement: LLM spend is difficult to trace across application call sites. This skill routes supported clients through Caveman Cloud and verifies one measured request.
actual_capabilities: Searches dependency files and source code for supported LLM client call sites.
Derives a valid application slug from existing package or module metadata.
Configures OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI, LangChain, LiteLLM, and raw HTTP clients.
Supports stored provider credentials and bring-your-own-key routing modes.
Sends one minimal request and reports HTTP status, model, and token usage.
limitations: Requires Caveman gateway, dashboard, credential mode, and API key values.
Routes prompt and response data through a third-party service.
BYOK mode exposes provider credentials to the Caveman gateway.
Verification creates one real provider request and may incur a small charge.

use_cases.title: Measure Application LLM Spend
use_cases.description: Route production application calls through one gateway and group measured spend by application slug.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Integrations
use_cases.description: Apply consistent gateway configuration across supported SDKs while preserving each call site's provider behavior.

use_cases.title: Verify Cost Observability
use_cases.description: Send a minimal request and confirm that status, model, token usage, and dashboard traces are available.

prompt_templates.title: Find Supported Call Sites
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository for live LLM call sites. List each file and line, but do not modify anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Caveman Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the detected LLM clients and propose the smallest Caveman routing changes. Explain credential handling for stored and BYOK modes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure and Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure all supported LLM call sites with my provided Caveman values. Ask before sending the billable verification request.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Mixed SDK Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this mixed OpenAI, Anthropic, and LangChain repository. Route every live call, preserve behavior, verify usage, and report unresolved coverage.

output_examples.input: Inspect a TypeScript service that uses the OpenAI SDK and prepare Caveman routing.
output_examples.output: Found one OpenAI call site. Proposed a gateway base URL, application slug, environment variables, and separate stored and BYOK credential handling.

output_examples.input: Verify an Anthropic integration after I approve one provider request.
output_examples.output: Verification completed with the observed HTTP status, model, input tokens, output tokens, routing mode, and dashboard trace location.

output_examples.input: Check a repository with no LLM dependencies or provider calls.
output_examples.output: No live LLM call sites were found. No files were changed and no verification request was sent.

best_practices: Review every detected call site before changing repository files.
Use scoped credentials, gitignored environment files, and the stored-key mode when possible.
Confirm the gateway destination and billable request before verification.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode gateway or provider credentials in source files.
Do not claim successful measurement without an observed response and usage values.
Do not fetch mutable instructions and apply them without revision or integrity checks.

faq.question: Which LLM clients are supported?
faq.answer: The instructions cover OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI, LangChain, LangGraph, LiteLLM, and raw provider-compatible HTTP calls.

faq.question: Does the skill change model behavior?
faq.answer: It targets record-mode routing and does not enable optimization. A gateway intermediary can still affect availability, privacy, and latency.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: Caveman credentials use the repository's existing gitignored environment file. Stored mode keeps provider credentials in Caveman Cloud.

faq.question: What happens in BYOK mode?
faq.answer: The application forwards its existing provider credential through the Caveman gateway for upstream authentication.

faq.question: Does verification cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. Verification sends one small real provider request, so the provider may charge for its tokens.

faq.question: What happens when no LLM call sites are found?
faq.answer: The skill stops without creating an integration or sending a verification request, then reports that nothing was available to route.
